claim_being_audited: Whether certifying the current model release is compliant because aggregate readiness passed, no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred, and the immigration-services intake weakness can be handled through current release documentation as a disclosed limitation.
decision_criteria: If current release documentation explicitly reflects the current evaluation results and clearly discloses the immigration-services intake weakness as a material limitation, certification could be compliant.
If there is approved mitigation or reviewed risk acceptance covering that subgroup weakness, certification could also be compliant.
If neither current disclosure nor approved mitigation exists in the release record, certification is not policy-compliant.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents are supportive but not sufficient to satisfy the policy when a material segment weakness remains unresolved.
evidence_requests: The current model card or release documentation section showing the immigration-services intake weakness is explicitly disclosed as a material limitation.
The current evaluation report for the release, including the segment-level result showing the 1.4 percentage point shortfall and how it is represented in release materials.
Any approved mitigation, owner acceptance, or reviewed risk-acceptance record covering this named launch use case.
The final certification packet version used for the release decision, not just a summary of its intended framing.
specific_concerns: The policy requires current release documentation to reflect current evaluation results and disclose material segment weaknesses or show approved mitigation.
The available summary confirms a current subgroup gap for the immigration-services intake slice and says the current record contains only an informal monitoring comment.
No admissible evidence in the summary shows that the current release documentation actually discloses this weakness as a material limitation.
No admissible evidence shows reviewed mitigation or approved risk acceptance for the subgroup weakness.
Prior model-family approval is explicitly contextual only under both the actor summary and policy text and cannot close the missing support link.
unsupported_claims: That certification is presently compliant on the existing record rather than only potentially defensible if the current documentation is updated to disclose the subgroup weakness.
That the subgroup weakness is already adequately covered by current release materials.
Any implication that prior approval or informal monitoring substitutes for current disclosure or approved mitigation.
